label: End of long (L=8-9) inputs, last original token / <DEL>, when sequence starts with k/2/w and contains s,f,x,r,i
predicate: (L >= 8) & (t >= 8) & (phase < 2) & isin(first_tok, [tok("k"), tok("2"), tok("w")]) & (n_seen([tok("s"), tok("f"), tok("x"), tok("r"), tok("i")]) >= 2)
explanation: Sparse feature that fires only at the end of the input phase in long sequences: the <DEL> step (60% of mass) or the last original token (40%), at t=8 or 9, almost only for L=8 or 9 (L=9 holds 86% of mass). It never fires in the copy phase after <DEL>, and never on earlier positions or shorter sequences. Among these end-of-input steps it fires on only about 0.6%. Which ones depends on the content of the sequence: the first token is strongly enriched for k (15x lift, 55% of mass), then 2 and w, and the earlier inputs are enriched for s, f, x, r, i. The strongest activations are on a final original token 1 (6x lift, 27% of mass; the top example k 0 3 s s f v r 1 has 4.5 max), with a weaker activation at the <DEL> that follows. Requiring the k/2/w start plus at least 2 of s/f/x/r/i keeps about 61% of activations and 66% of mass, but precision is only about 11%, so the content dependence looks like a fuzzy combination of tokens that a simple predicate does not capture. Boundary alone (L>=8, t>=8, not copy phase) gives 97% recall at 0.6% precision.
